title.zh: 卷二十二 梁臣傳第十: 康懷英 劉鄩 牛存節 張歸霸 王重師 徐懷玉
title.en: Volume 22 Later Liang Biographies 2: Kang Huaiying, Liu Xun, Niu Cunjie, Zhang Guiba, Wang Zhongshi, Xu Huaiyu
title.raw: 卷二十二 梁臣傳第十: 康懷英 劉鄩 牛存節 張歸霸 王重師 徐懷玉 Volume 22 Later Liang Biographies 2: Kang Huaiying, Liu Xun, Niu Cunjie, Zhang Guiba, Wang Zhongshi, Xu Huaiyu

sentences.zh: 康懷英

translations.literal: Kang Huaiying
translations.idiomatic: Kang Huaiying

sentences.zh: 康懷英，兗州人也。

translations.literal: Kang Huaiying was a native of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Huaiying came from Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 事朱瑾為牙將，梁兵攻瑾，瑾出略食豐、沛間，留懷英守城，懷英即以城降梁，瑾遂奔於吳。

translations.literal: He served Zhu Jin as a junior general; when Liang troops attacked Jin, Jin went out to forage between Feng and Pei and left Huaiying to hold the city; Huaiying at once surrendered the city to Liang, and Jin then fled to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He served Zhu Jin as a junior officer. When Liang attacked, Jin rode out to forage in Feng and Pei and left Huaiying to hold the city; Huaiying opened the gates to Liang, and Jin fled to Wu.

sentences.zh: 太祖得懷英，大喜。

translations.literal: Taizu of Liang obtained Huaiying and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu of Liang took Huaiying into his service and rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 後從氏叔琮攻趙匡凝，下鄧州。

translations.literal: Later he followed Shi Shucong in attacking Zhao Kuangning and took Deng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Shi Shucong against Zhao Kuangning and captured Deng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 梁兵攻李茂貞於岐，以懷英為先鋒，至武功，擊殺岐兵萬餘人，太祖喜曰：「邑名武功，真武功也。

translations.literal: Liang troops attacked Li Maozhen at Qi; Huaiying was made vanguard; reaching Wugong, they struck and killed more than ten thousand Qi troops; Taizu rejoiced and said: “The place is named Wugong—truly martial achievement!
translations.idiomatic: When Liang attacked Li Maozhen at Qi, Huaiying led the vanguard. At Wugong he killed more than ten thousand Qi troops. Taizu was delighted: “The place is called Wugong—and true martial deeds were done there!

sentences.zh: 」以名馬賜之。

translations.literal: ” He gave him a famous horse as reward.
translations.idiomatic: ” He rewarded him with a famous horse.

sentences.zh: 是時，李周彜以鄜坊兵救岐，屯於三原界，懷英擊走之，因取其翟州而還。

translations.literal: At that time Li Zhouyi came with Bin-Fang troops to rescue Qi and encamped on the border at Sanyuan; Huaiying routed him and on returning seized his Zhai prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhouyi then marched from Bin and Fang to relieve Qi and camped on the Sanyuan frontier; Huaiying drove him off and took Zhai prefecture on the way back.

sentences.zh: 岐兵屯奉天，懷英柵其東北。

translations.literal: Qi troops encamped at Fengtian; Huaiying palisaded northeast of them.
translations.idiomatic: Qi forces held Fengtian; Huaiying fortified to their northeast.

sentences.zh: 夜半，岐兵攻之，懷英以為夜中不欲驚它軍，獨以三千人出戰，遲明，岐兵解去，身被十餘瘡。

translations.literal: At midnight Qi troops attacked; Huaiying, thinking he should not alarm the other armies in the night, went out alone with three thousand men to fight; at dawn the Qi troops withdrew; he was wounded in more than ten places.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight the Qi attacked. Not wanting to rouse the other camps in the dark, Huaiying went out with only three thousand men. By dawn the Qi withdrew; he bore more than ten wounds.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞與梁和，昭宗還京師，賜懷英「迎鑾毅勇功臣」。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen made peace with Liang; Emperor Zhaozong returned to the capital; Huaiying was granted the title Meritorious Brave of Welcoming the Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen made peace with Liang; Zhaozong returned to Chang’an; Huaiying was titled Meritorious Brave of Welcoming the Chariot.

sentences.zh: 楊行密攻宿州，太祖遣懷英擊走之，表宿州刺史。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi attacked Suzhou; Taizu sent Huaiying to rout him and memorialized him as prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xingmi attacked Suzhou, Taizu sent Huaiying to beat him back and had him appointed prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷保義軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military governor of the Baoyi army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military governor of Baoyi.

sentences.zh: 丁會以潞州叛梁降晉，太祖命懷英為招討使，將行，太祖戒之，語甚切，懷英惶恐，以謂潞州期必得，乃築夾城圍之。

translations.literal: Ding Hui rebelled against Liang at Luzhou and surrendered to Jin; Taizu appointed Huaiying pacification commissioner; as he was about to march, Taizu warned him in words very earnest; Huaiying was fearful and believed Luzhou must be taken; he therefore built twin fortifications to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Hui rebelled at Luzhou and went over to Jin. Taizu named Huaiying pacification commissioner and, before he marched, warned him sternly. Huaiying took the mission to heart, convinced Luzhou must fall, and built linked fortifications to starve the city.

sentences.zh: 晉遣周德威屯於亂柳，數攻夾城，懷英不敢出戰，太祖乃以李思安代懷英將，降懷英為都虞候。

translations.literal: Jin sent Zhou Dewei to encamp at Luanliu and repeatedly attacked the twin fortifications; Huaiying dared not go out to fight; Taizu then replaced Huaiying with Li Si’an as commander and demoted Huaiying to chief adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent Zhou Dewei to Luanliu and hammered the siege lines again and again; Huaiying would not leave the walls. Taizu replaced him with Li Si’an and reduced Huaiying to chief adjutant.

sentences.zh: 久之，思安亦無功，太祖大怒，罷思安，以同州劉知俊為招討使。

translations.literal: After a long time Si’an too achieved nothing; Taizu was greatly angered, dismissed Si’an, and made Liu Zhijun of Tongzhou pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Si’an also failed after long months; Taizu in fury removed him and put Liu Zhijun of Tongzhou in command.

sentences.zh: 知俊未至軍，太祖自至澤州，為懷英等軍援，且督之。

translations.literal: Before Zhijun reached the army, Taizu himself went to Ze prefecture to reinforce Huaiying’s troops and supervise them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun had not yet reached the front when Taizu himself went to Ze to reinforce Huaiying and drive the siege.

sentences.zh: 已而晉王李克用卒，莊宗召周德威還。

translations.literal: Before long Prince of Jin Li Keyong died and Zhuangzong recalled Zhou Dewei.
translations.idiomatic: Then Li Keyong died and Zhuangzong called Zhou Dewei home.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞晉有喪，德威去，亦歸洛陽，而諸將亦少弛。

translations.literal: Taizu heard that Jin was in mourning and that Dewei had gone; he too returned to Luoyang, and the generals also slackened somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Jin was in mourning and Dewei had left, Taizu withdrew to Luoyang and his generals eased their grip.

sentences.zh: 莊宗謂德威曰：「晉之所以能敵梁，而彼所憚者，先王也。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong told Dewei: “Jin’s ability to match Liang—what they fear is my late father.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong told Dewei: “Jin can stand against Liang only because they fear my father.

sentences.zh: 今聞吾王之喪，謂我新立，未能出兵，其意必怠，宜出其不意以擊之，非徒解圍，亦足以定霸也。

translations.literal: Now that they hear my king has died, they will think I am newly enthroned and cannot send troops; their guard must slacken; we should strike where they do not expect—not merely lift the siege but also fix hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: Now they hear he is dead and think me too new to march. They will grow careless. Strike before they expect it—not only to break the siege but to settle the balance of power.

sentences.zh: 」乃與德威等疾馳六日至北黃碾，會天大昏霧，伏兵三垂岡，直趨夾城，攻破之。

translations.literal: ” He then galloped with Dewei and the rest six days to North Huangnian; they met a great dark fog; they lay ambush at Sanchuigang, rushed straight at the twin fortifications, and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: ” He and Dewei raced six days to North Huangnian. A thick fog covered the field; they hid at Sanchuigang, then drove straight at the twin fortifications and smashed them.

sentences.zh: 懷英大敗，亡大將三百人，懷英以百騎遁歸，詣闕請死。

translations.literal: Huaiying was routed; three hundred great generals were lost; Huaiying escaped with a hundred horsemen, went to court, and asked for death.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiying was shattered; three hundred senior officers fell; he fled with a hundred riders, reached court, and begged to die.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「去歲興兵，太陰虧食，占者以為不利，吾獨違之而致敗，非爾過也。

translations.literal: Taizu said: “Last year when we raised troops the great yin was eclipsed; diviners said it was unfavorable; I alone went against them and met defeat—not your fault.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said: “Last year the moon was eaten when we took the field; the diviners called it ill omen. I alone defied them and lost—not your fault.

sentences.zh: 」釋之，以為右衛上將軍。

translations.literal: ” He released him and made him Right Guard General-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: ” He pardoned him and made him Right Guard General-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 劉知俊叛，奔於岐，以懷英為保義軍節度使、西路副招討使。

translations.literal: When Liu Zhijun rebelled and fled to Qi, Huaiying was made military governor of the Baoyi army and deputy western-route pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhijun rebelled and fled to Qi, Huaiying was made military governor of Baoyi and deputy western-route pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 知俊以岐兵圍靈武，太祖遣懷英攻邠寧以牽之。

translations.literal: Zhijun with Qi troops besieged Lingwu; Taizu sent Huaiying to attack Bin and Ning to draw him off.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun and the Qi besieged Lingwu; Taizu sent Huaiying against Bin and Ning to pull him away.

sentences.zh: 懷英取寧、慶、衍三州，還至升平，知俊掩擊之，懷英大敗。

translations.literal: Huaiying took the three prefectures Ning, Qing, and Yan; on returning to Shengping, Zhijun ambushed him and Huaiying was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiying took Ning, Qing, and Yan, but on the march back through Shengping Zhijun struck from cover and broke him.

sentences.zh: 徙鎮感化。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Ganhua.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to Ganhua.

sentences.zh: 其後朱友謙叛附於晉，以懷英討之，與晉人戰白徑嶺，懷英又大敗。

translations.literal: Later Zhu Youqian rebelled and joined Jin; Huaiying was sent against him; he fought the Jin at Baijing Ridge and was routed again.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Youqian rebelled and went over to Jin, Huaiying was sent against him, met the Jin at Baijing Ridge, and lost again.

sentences.zh: 徙鎮永平，卒於鎮。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Yongping and died in post.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to Yongping and died there.

sentences.zh: 劉鄩，密州安丘人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xun
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun

sentences.zh: 少事青州王敬武。

translations.literal: Liu Xun was a native of Anqiu in Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun came from Anqiu in Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 敬武卒，子師範立。

translations.literal: In youth he served Wang Jingwu of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served Wang Jingwu of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 棣州刺史張蟾叛，師範遣指揮使盧洪討蟾，洪亦叛。

translations.literal: Jingwu died and his son Shifan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingwu died, his son Shifan took his place.

sentences.zh: 師範偽為好辭召洪，洪至，迎於郊外，命鄩斬之座上，因使鄩攻張蟾，破之。

translations.literal: Tizhou prefect Zhang Chan rebelled; Shifan sent the commander Lu Hong to suppress Chan; Hong rebelled as well.
translations.idiomatic: Tizhou prefect Zhang Chan rose in revolt; Shifan sent Lu Hong to crush him—and Hong rebelled too.

sentences.zh: 師範表鄩登州刺史，以為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Shifan with false kind words summoned Hong; when Hong arrived and was welcomed in the suburbs, he ordered Xun to behead him at table; he then sent Xun against Zhang Chan and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan lured Hong with fair words and received him in the suburbs; at the feast he had Xun cut off Hong’s head, then sent Xun against Zhang Chan and broke him.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖西攻鳳翔，師範乘梁虛，陰遣人分襲梁諸州縣，它遣者謀多漏泄，事不成。

translations.literal: Shifan memorialized Xun as prefect of Dengzhou and made him march chief of staff.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan had Xun appointed prefect of Deng and made him chief of staff on campaign.

sentences.zh: 獨鄩素好兵書，有機略。

translations.literal: Taizu of Liang attacked Fengxiang in the west; Shifan, exploiting Liang’s emptiness, secretly sent men to raid Liang’s prefectures and counties; the other envoys’ plots often leaked and the affairs failed.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu of Liang marched west against Fengxiang, Shifan struck at Liang’s empty rear, sending raiders against its prefectures and counties; other agents’ plans leaked and came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 是時，梁已破朱瑾等，悉有兗、鄆，以葛從周為兗州節度使，從周將兵在外，鄩乃使人負油鬻城中，悉視城中虛實出入之所。

translations.literal: Only Xun had long loved military books and possessed stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Only Xun had studied the art of war and knew how to scheme.

sentences.zh: 油者得羅城下水竇可入，鄩乃以步兵五百從水竇襲破之，徙從周家屬外第，親拜其母，撫之甚有恩禮。

translations.literal: At that time Liang had already broken Zhu Jin and the rest and fully held Yan and Yun; Ge Congzhou was military governor of Yanzhou; Congzhou led troops abroad; Xun had men carry oil and sell it in the city and fully observed the city’s empty and full points and paths in and out.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had already broken Zhu Jin and held Yan and Yun. Ge Congzhou governed Yanzhou while his army was away; Xun sent men to peddle oil in the city and mapped every weak point and gate.

sentences.zh: 太祖已出昭宗於鳳翔，引兵東還，遣朱友寧攻師範、從周攻鄩。

translations.literal: The oil sellers found a water gate under the outer wall by which one could enter; Xun then with five hundred infantry entered through the water gate and stormed the city; he moved Congzhou’s family to an outer mansion, personally visited his mother, and treated her with great kindness and ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The peddlers found a drain under the outer wall wide enough to enter; Xun sent five hundred foot soldiers through it and took the city. He moved Congzhou’s family to a house outside the walls, bowed to Congzhou’s mother, and treated her with every courtesy.

sentences.zh: 鄩以版輿置從周母城上，母呼從周曰：「劉將軍待我甚厚，無異於汝。

translations.literal: Taizu had already escorted Emperor Zhaozong from Fengxiang and was returning east with troops; he sent Zhu Youning to attack Shifan and Congzhou to attack Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had brought Zhaozong out of Fengxiang and was marching east; he sent Zhu Youning against Shifan and Ge Congzhou against Xun.

sentences.zh: 人臣各為其主，汝可察之！

translations.literal: Xun placed Congzhou’s mother on a palanquin on the city wall; the mother called to Congzhou: “General Liu treats me very well—no different from you.
translations.idiomatic: Xun set Congzhou’s mother in a litter on the wall; she called down: “General Liu has treated me as kindly as you would.

sentences.zh: 」從周為之緩攻。

translations.literal: Each minister serves his own lord—you should weigh that!
translations.idiomatic: Every man serves his master—think on that!

sentences.zh: 鄩乃悉簡婦人及民之老疾不足當敵者出之，獨與少壯者同辛苦，分衣食，堅守以待。

translations.literal: ” Congzhou therefore eased his attack; Xun then selected out all women and townspeople old or sick and unable to fight; he alone shared hardship with the strong young, divided food and clothing, and held firm waiting.
translations.idiomatic: ” Congzhou slackened the assault. Xun sent out every woman and every old or sick man who could not fight, shared rations and labor with the able-bodied, and held on.

sentences.zh: 外援不至，人心頗離，副使王彥溫逾城而奔，守陴者多逸。

translations.literal: External aid did not arrive; hearts grew unsettled; the deputy Wang Yanwen crossed the wall and fled, and many on the walls deserted.
translations.idiomatic: Relief never came; morale frayed; deputy Wang Yanwen slipped over the wall and fled, and many defenders followed.

sentences.zh: 鄩乃遣人陽語彥溫曰：「副使勿多以人出，非吾素遣者，皆勿以行。

translations.literal: Xun then sent a man with feigned words to Yanwen: “Deputy, do not take too many out; those not envoys I usually send—none may go.
translations.idiomatic: Xun sent a man to Yanwen with a false message: “Deputy, do not let too many leave. Anyone not sent by me must stay.

sentences.zh: 」又下令城中曰：「吾遣從副使者得出，否者皆族。

translations.literal: ” He also ordered in the city: “Those I send following the deputy may go out; otherwise their clans will be exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: ” He also proclaimed in the city: “Only those the deputy escorts for me may leave; anyone else who flees loses his whole clan.

sentences.zh: 」城中皆惑，奔者乃止。

translations.literal: ” The people in the city were all confused and the flight then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: ” The city was thrown into confusion and the panic subsided.

sentences.zh: 已而梁兵聞之，果疑彥溫非實降者，斬之城下，由是城守益堅。

translations.literal: Before long the Liang troops heard of it; they indeed suspected Yanwen was not a true surrender and beheaded him below the wall; from this the city’s defense grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang heard the story they decided Yanwen’s surrender was a trick and cut off his head beneath the wall; after that the defense hardened.

sentences.zh: 師範兵已屈，從周以禍福諭鄩，鄩報曰：「俟吾主降，即以城還梁。

translations.literal: Shifan’s troops were already bent; Congzhou with fortune and disaster persuaded Xun; Xun replied: “Wait until my lord surrenders and I will return the city to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan’s army was failing; Congzhou tried to win Xun with threats and promises. Xun answered: “When my master yields, I will hand the city to Liang.

sentences.zh: 」師範敗，降梁，鄩乃亦降。

translations.literal: ” Shifan was defeated and surrendered to Liang; Xun then surrendered as well.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shifan was beaten and submitted; Xun surrendered too.

sentences.zh: 從周為具賫裝，送鄩歸梁，鄩曰：「降將蒙梁恩不誅，幸矣，敢乘馬而衣裘乎！

translations.literal: Congzhou prepared gifts and escort and sent Xun back to Liang; Xun said: “A surrendered general who receives Liang’s grace and is not killed is fortunate enough—how dare I ride a horse and wear fur!
translations.idiomatic: Congzhou fitted him out and sent him to Liang. Xun said: “A beaten man spared by Liang is already lucky—how dare I ride a horse and wear fine furs?

sentences.zh: 」乃素服乘驢歸梁。

translations.literal: ” He then in plain dress rode a donkey back to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: ” He went in plain clothes on a donkey.

sentences.zh: 太祖賜之冠帶，飲之以酒，鄩辭以量小，太祖曰：「取兗州，量何大乎？

translations.literal: Taizu bestowed cap and belt and treated him with wine; Xun declined on grounds of small capacity; Taizu said: “When you took Yanzhou—what great capacity was that?
translations.idiomatic: Taizu gave him cap and belt and poured wine; Xun pleaded a weak head for drink. Taizu said: “You took Yanzhou—was that the act of a small man?

sentences.zh: 」以為元從都押衙。

translations.literal: ” He made him chief adjutant of the original followers.
translations.idiomatic: ” He made him chief adjutant of the original followers.

sentences.zh: 是時，太祖已領四鎮，將吏皆功臣舊人，鄩一旦以降將居其上，及諸將見鄩，皆用軍禮，鄩居自如，太祖益奇之。

translations.literal: At that time Taizu already held four circuits; officers and men were all meritorious old companions; Xun suddenly as a surrendered general stood above them; when the generals saw Xun they all used military ritual; Xun remained composed; Taizu admired him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu already commanded four circuits; his officers were old companions in merit. Xun, a fresh surrender, sat above them; every general saluted by military rite, and Xun took it as his due—Taizu marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，累遷左龍武統軍。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, Xun was repeatedly promoted to Left Dragon Martial Commander.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizu’s accession Xun rose to Left Dragon Martial Commander.

sentences.zh: 劉知俊叛，陷長安，太祖遣鄩與牛存節討之，知俊走鳳翔，太祖乃以長安為永平軍，拜鄩節度使。

translations.literal: When Liu Zhijun rebelled and took Chang’an, Taizu sent Xun and Niu Cunjie against him; Zhijun fled to Fengxiang; Taizu then made Chang’an the Yongping army and enfeoffed Xun its military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhijun rebelled and seized Chang’an, Taizu sent Xun and Niu Cunjie against him. Zhijun fled to Fengxiang; Taizu made Chang’an the Yongping circuit and gave Xun its governorship.

sentences.zh: 末帝即位，領鎮南軍節度使，為開封尹。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, Xun held the Zhennan army as military governor and served as intendant of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Last Emperor he governed Zhennan and served as intendant of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 楊師厚卒，分相、魏為兩鎮，末帝恐魏兵亂，遣鄩以兵屯於魏縣。

translations.literal: When Yang Shihou died, Xiang and Wei were split into two circuits; the Last Emperor feared turmoil among the Wei troops and sent Xun with an army to encamp at Wei county.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Shihou died the court split Xiang and Wei into two commands. Fearing mutiny in Wei, the Last Emperor sent Xun to camp at Wei county.

sentences.zh: 魏兵果亂，劫賀德倫降晉。

translations.literal: The Wei troops indeed rebelled and coerced He Delun into surrendering to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei soldiers did rise, forced He Delun’s hand, and went over to Jin.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入魏，鄩以謂晉兵悉從莊宗赴魏，而太原可襲，乃結草為人，執以旗幟，以驢負之往來城上，而潛軍出黃澤關襲太原。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong entered Wei; Xun judged that the Jin troops had all followed Zhuangzong to Wei while Taiyuan could be raided; he made straw men, set them with flags and banners, had donkeys carry them back and forth on the wall, and secretly sent his army out through Huangze Pass to raid Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong entered Wei. Xun reasoned that every Jin soldier had followed him there and that Taiyuan lay open; he mounted straw dummies with flags on donkeys and marched them along the walls while his army slipped out through Huangze Pass toward Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 晉兵望梁壘旗幟往來，不知其去也，以故不追。

translations.literal: The Jin troops saw Liang ramparts with flags moving back and forth and did not know they had gone; therefore they did not pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Jin lookouts saw banners still moving on the Liang walls and never guessed the camp was empty; they did not pursue.

sentences.zh: 鄩至樂平，遇雨，不克進而旋，急趨臨清，爭魏積粟，而周德威已先至，鄩乃屯於莘縣，築甬道及河以饋軍。

translations.literal: Xun reached Leeping, met rain, could not advance and turned back; he hurried to Linqing to contest Wei’s stored grain, but Zhou Dewei had already arrived first; Xun then encamped at Shen county, built a corridor road to the river, and fed his army.
translations.idiomatic: Rain stopped Xun at Leeping and forced him back. He raced to Linqing for Wei’s grain stores, but Zhou Dewei was already there; Xun fell back to Shen county, built a supply road to the river, and fed his men.

sentences.zh: 久之，末帝以書責鄩曰：「閫外之事全付將軍，河朔諸州一旦淪沒。

translations.literal: After a long time the Last Emperor with a letter blamed Xun: “Matters beyond the pass I wholly entrusted to you, general; the Hebei prefectures were lost in a day.
translations.idiomatic: Months later the Last Emperor wrote in rebuke: “I gave you full command beyond the pass, and Hebei fell in a day.

sentences.zh: 今倉儲已竭，飛免不充，將軍與國同心，宜思良畫！

translations.literal: Now the stores are exhausted and urgent relief cannot fill them; general, be of one mind with the state and think of a good plan!
translations.idiomatic: Stores are empty and no convoy can refill them. Stand with the throne and find a way forward!

sentences.zh: 」鄩報曰：「晉兵甚銳，未可擊，宜待之。

translations.literal: ” Xun replied: “The Jin troops are very sharp; they cannot be struck; we should wait.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xun answered: “Jin is too keen to fight now. Wait.

sentences.zh: 」末帝復遣問鄩必勝之策，鄩曰：「臣無奇術，請人給米十斛，米盡則敵破矣！

translations.literal: ” The Last Emperor again sent to ask Xun’s plan for certain victory; Xun said: “Your servant has no strange art; please give each man ten hu of rice—when the rice is gone the enemy will be broken!
translations.idiomatic: ” The Last Emperor asked again for a sure plan. Xun said: “I have no trick—only give every man ten hu of grain. When the grain is gone, the enemy breaks.

sentences.zh: 」末帝大怒，誚鄩曰：「將軍蓄米，將療饑乎？

translations.literal: ” The Last Emperor was greatly angered and reproached Xun: “General, are you hoarding rice to cure hunger?
translations.idiomatic: ” The Last Emperor raged: “Are you stockpiling rice to feed yourselves?

sentences.zh: 將破敵乎？

translations.literal: Or to break the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: Or to break the enemy?

sentences.zh: 」乃遣使者監督其軍。

translations.literal: ” He then sent an envoy to supervise his army.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent overseers to the camp.

sentences.zh: 鄩召諸將謀曰：「主上深居禁中，與白面兒謀，必敗人事。

translations.literal: Xun summoned the generals to plan and said: “The sovereign deep in the inner palace plots with pale-faced boys—he is sure to ruin affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xun called his officers and said: “The emperor sits in the inner palace taking counsel from soft-faced courtiers—he will ruin this war.

sentences.zh: 今敵盛，未可輕動，諸君以為如何？

translations.literal: Now the enemy is strong and cannot be lightly moved; gentlemen, what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is strong; we must not stir rashly. What say you?

sentences.zh: 」諸將皆欲戰，鄩乃悉召諸將坐之軍門，人以河水一杯飲之，諸將莫測，或飲或辭，鄩曰：「一杯之難猶若此，滔滔河流可盡乎？

translations.literal: The generals all wished to fight; Xun then summoned all the generals to sit at the army gate, gave each a cup of river water to drink; the generals could not fathom it; some drank and some declined; Xun said: “If one cup is this hard, can the surging river be exhausted?
translations.idiomatic: They all wanted battle. Xun seated them at the gate and gave each a cup of river water. Some drank, some refused, baffled. Xun said: “One cup is hard enough—can you drink the whole Yellow River?

sentences.zh: 」諸將皆失色。

translations.literal: ” The generals all changed color.
translations.idiomatic: ” Every face went pale.

sentences.zh: 是時，莊宗在魏，數以勁兵壓鄩營，鄩不肯出，而末帝又數促鄩，使出戰。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuangzong was at Wei and repeatedly pressed strong troops against Xun’s camp; Xun would not come out, yet the Last Emperor again repeatedly urged Xun to go out and fight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong at Wei kept sending crack troops against Xun’s lines; Xun would not budge, but the Last Emperor kept ordering him out.

sentences.zh: 莊宗與諸將謀曰：「劉鄩學《六韜》，喜以機變用兵，本欲示弱以襲我，今其見迫，必求速戰。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong planned with his generals: “Liu Xun studied the Six Secret Teachings and loves to use stratagem in war; he originally meant to show weakness and surprise us; now that he is pressed he must seek a quick battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong told his officers: “Xun knows the Six Secret Teachings and lives by surprise. He wanted to look weak and trap us; now that he is harried he will have to fight fast.

sentences.zh: 」乃聲言歸太原，命符存審守魏，陽為西歸，而潛兵貝州。

translations.literal: ” He then publicly announced return to Taiyuan, ordered Fu Cunjian to hold Wei, feigned a westward return, and secretly moved troops to Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: ” He announced a march back to Taiyuan, left Fu Cunjian at Wei, pretended to go west, and hid his army at Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 鄩果報末帝曰：「晉王西歸，魏無備，可擊。

translations.literal: Xun indeed reported to the Last Emperor: “The Prince of Jin has returned west; Wei is unguarded and can be struck.
translations.idiomatic: Xun reported to the Last Emperor: “Zhuangzong has gone west; Wei is bare—we can hit it.

sentences.zh: 」乃以兵萬人攻魏城東，莊宗自貝州返趨擊之。

translations.literal: ” He then with ten thousand troops attacked the east of Wei city; Zhuangzong returned from Beizhou and rushed to intercept.
translations.idiomatic: ” He marched ten thousand men against the east wall of Wei; Zhuangzong wheeled from Beizhou and struck.

sentences.zh: 鄩忽見晉軍，驚曰：「晉王在此邪！

translations.literal: Xun suddenly saw the Jin army and startled: “The Prince of Jin is here!
translations.idiomatic: Xun saw the Jin host and cried: “Zhuangzong—here?

sentences.zh: 」兵稍卻，追至故元城，莊宗與符存審為兩方陣夾之，鄩為圓陣以禦晉人。

translations.literal: ” The troops slightly retreated; pursued to old Yuancheng, Zhuangzong and Fu Cunjian with two square formations flanked him; Xun formed a circle to resist the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: ” His line buckled. Pursued to old Yuancheng, Zhuangzong and Fu Cunjian closed on him from two sides; Xun drew a circle to meet Jin steel.

sentences.zh: 兵再合，鄩大敗，南奔，自黎陽濟河，保滑州。

translations.literal: The armies joined twice; Xun was routed; he fled south, crossed the river from Liyang, and held Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: They clashed twice; Xun broke; he ran south, crossed at Liyang, and held Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 末帝以為義成軍節度使。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor made him military governor of the Yicheng army.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor made him military governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 明年，河朔皆入於晉，降鄩亳州團練使。

translations.literal: The next year Hebei all entered Jin; Xun was demoted to regiment trainer of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Hebei fell to Jin; Xun was reduced to regiment trainer at Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 兗州張萬進反，拜鄩兗州安撫制置使。

translations.literal: Zhang Wanjin of Yanzhou rebelled; Xun was enfeoffed pacification commissioner of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Wanjin rebelled at Yanzhou, Xun was named Yanzhou pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 萬進敗死，乃拜鄩泰寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: Wanjin was defeated and died; Xun was then enfeoffed military governor of the Taining army.
translations.idiomatic: Wanjin was beaten and killed; Xun was then made military governor of Taining.

sentences.zh: 朱友謙叛，陷同州，末帝以鄩為河東道招討使，行次陜州，鄩為書以招友謙，友謙不報，留月余待之。

translations.literal: Zhu Youqian rebelled and took Tongzhou; the Last Emperor made Xun Hedong-route pacification commissioner; on the march at Shaan prefecture, Xun wrote a letter to win Youqian over; Youqian did not answer; he stayed more than a month waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Youqian rebelled and seized Tongzhou, the Last Emperor sent Xun as Hedong-route pacification commissioner. At Shaan he wrote to win Youqian over; Youqian never answered, and Xun waited more than a month.

sentences.zh: 尹皓、段凝等素惡鄩，乃譖之，以為鄩與友謙親家，故其逗留以養賊。

translations.literal: Yin Hao, Duan Ning, and the rest had long hated Xun; they slandered him, saying Xun and Youqian were in-laws and therefore delayed to nurture the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao, Duan Ning, and others had long hated him; they whispered that Xun and Youqian were kin by marriage and that he was stalling to feed the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 已而鄩兵數敗，乃罷鄩歸洛陽，冘殺之，年六十四，贈中書令。

translations.literal: Before long Xun’s troops were repeatedly defeated; he was dismissed and returned to Luoyang and secretly killed; he was sixty-four; posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His army lost again and again; he was recalled to Luoyang and quietly executed at sixty-four; posthumously he was made Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子遂凝、遂雍，事唐皆為刺史。

translations.literal: His sons Sui Ning and Sui Yong both served Tang as prefects.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Sui Ning and Sui Yong both served Tang as prefects.

sentences.zh: 鄩妾王氏有美色，鄩卒後，入明宗宮中，是為王淑妃。

translations.literal: Xun’s concubine Lady Wang had beautiful looks; after Xun died she entered Mingzong’s palace and became Wang Shufei.
translations.idiomatic: Xun’s concubine Lady Wang was famed for her beauty; after his death she entered Mingzong’s palace as Wang Shufei.

sentences.zh: 明宗晚年，淑妃用事，鄩二子皆被恩寵。

translations.literal: In Mingzong’s later years Shufei held power; Xun’s two sons both received favor and grace.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingzong’s last years Shufei ruled from behind the screen; both of Xun’s sons basked in favor.

sentences.zh: 潞王從珂反於鳳翔，時遂雍為西京副留守，留守王思同率諸鎮兵討鳳翔，戰敗東歸，遂雍閉門不內，悉封府庫以待潞王。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu Congke rebelled at Fengxiang, Sui Yong was then deputy intendant of the Western Capital; intendant Wang Sitong led the troops of the various circuits against Fengxiang; defeated, he returned east; Sui Yong closed the gates and would not admit him, fully sealed the treasury, and waited for the Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Congke, Prince of Lu, rose at Fengxiang, Sui Yong was deputy intendant of the Western Capital. Wang Sitong marched the circuit armies against him, was beaten, and retreated east; Sui Yong shut the gates, sealed the treasury, and waited for Congke.

sentences.zh: 潞王前軍至者，悉以金帛給之。

translations.literal: To the Prince of Lu’s advance troops who arrived, he gave all gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: He paid out gold and silk to every vanguard unit that arrived.

sentences.zh: 潞王見遂雍，握手流涕，由是事無大小皆與圖議。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu saw Sui Yong he clasped hands and wept; from this, affairs great and small were all discussed with him.
translations.idiomatic: Congke met Sui Yong with clasped hands and tears; from then on every weighty matter passed through him.

sentences.zh: 廢帝入立，拜遂雍淄州刺史，以鄩兄琪之子遂清代遂雍為西京副留守。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor entered and took the throne, Sui Yong was enfeoffed prefect of Zibo; Sui Qing, son of Xun’s elder brother Qi, replaced Sui Yong as deputy intendant of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Sui Yong was made prefect of Zibo; Sui Qing, son of Xun’s elder brother Qi, replaced him as deputy intendant of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 遂清歷易、棣等五州刺史，皆有善政，遷鳳州防禦使、宣徽北院使，判三司。

translations.literal: Sui Qing successively governed Yizhou, Tizhou, and five prefectures in all, all with good governance; he was promoted to defense commissioner of Feng prefecture, commissioner of the Xuanhui North Court, and judge of the Three Bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Qing served in turn at Yizhou, Tizhou, and five prefectures, governing well at each; he rose to defense commissioner of Feng, commissioner of the Xuanhui North Court, and overseer of the Three Bureaus.

sentences.zh: 晉開運中為安州防禦使以卒。

translations.literal: In Jin’s Kaiyun era he served as Anzhou Defense Commissioner and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin’s Kaiyun reign he held Anzhou as defense commissioner and died in post.

sentences.zh: 遂清性至孝，居父喪哀毀，鄉里稱之。

translations.literal: Suo Qing was extremely filial; during his father’s mourning he was wasted by grief; the neighborhood praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Qing was profoundly filial; mourning his father he wasted away in grief, and neighbors praised him.

sentences.zh: 嘗為淄州刺史，迎其母，母及郊，遂清為母執轡行數十里，州人咸以為榮。

translations.literal: Once when he was Zibo prefect and went to meet his mother, when she reached the outskirts Suo Qing took the reins and walked several dozen li with her; the people of the prefecture all took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Zibo he went to meet his mother; when she reached the suburbs he took the reins and walked beside her carriage for miles—the whole prefecture counted it an honor.

sentences.zh: 牛存節

translations.literal: Niu Cunjie
translations.idiomatic: Niu Cunjie

sentences.zh: 牛存節，字贊正，青州博昌人也。

translations.literal: Niu Cunjie, styled Zanzheng, was a native of Bochang in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Cunjie, styled Zanzheng, came from Bochang in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初名禮，事諸葛爽於河陽，爽卒，存節顧其徒曰：「天下洶洶，當得英雄事之。

translations.literal: At first named Li, he served Zhuge Shuang at Heyang; when Shuang died, Cunjie looked at his followers and said: “The realm is in turmoil—we must find a hero to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Born Li, he served Zhuge Shuang at Heyang; when Shuang died he turned to his men: “The realm churns—we must find a hero to follow.

sentences.zh: 」乃率其徒十餘人歸梁太祖。

translations.literal: ” He then led more than ten of his followers to submit to Liang Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: ” He led a dozen followers to Liang Taizu.

sentences.zh: 存節為人木強忠謹，太祖愛之，賜之名字，以為小校。

translations.literal: Cunjie was stubbornly honest and loyal; Taizu loved him, bestowed on him his name, and made him a petty officer.
translations.idiomatic: Stubborn, loyal, and careful, Cunjie won Taizu’s affection; Taizu gave him his present name and made him a junior officer.

sentences.zh: 張至攻汴，存節破其二寨。

translations.literal: When Zhang Zhi attacked Bian, Cunjie broke two of his stockades.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhi struck at Bian, Cunjie smashed two of his camps.

sentences.zh: 梁攻濮州，戰南劉橋、範縣，存節功多。

translations.literal: When Liang attacked Puzhou, fighting at Nan Liu Bridge and Fan County, Cunjie won much merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang’s assault on Puzhou, at Nan Liu Bridge and Fan County, Cunjie earned the lion’s share of the credit.

sentences.zh: 李罕之圍張全義於河陽，全義乞兵於梁，太祖以存節故事河陽，知其間道，使以兵為前鋒。

translations.literal: Li Hanzhi besieged Zhang Quanyi at Heyang; Quanyi asked Liang for troops; Taizu, because Cunjie had formerly served at Heyang and knew the bypaths, sent him as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanzhi besieged Zhang Quanyi at Heyang; Quanyi begged Liang for help; Taizu knew Cunjie had served there before and knew the back roads, and sent him ahead as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 是時歲饑，兵行乏食，存節以金帛就民易幹葚以食軍，擊走罕之。

translations.literal: At the time famine reigned; the army lacked food; Cunjie exchanged gold and silk with the people for dried mulberries to feed the troops and drove off Hanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Famine year—the army ran short of food; Cunjie traded gold and cloth to villagers for dried mulberries to feed his men, then routed Hanzhi.

sentences.zh: 太祖攻魏，存節下魏黎陽、臨河，殺魏萬二千人，與太祖會內黃。

translations.literal: When Taizu attacked Wei, Cunjie took Wei’s Liyang and Linhe, killed twelve thousand Wei troops, and joined Taizu at Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizu’s assault on Wei, Cunjie took Liyang and Linhe, killed twelve thousand Wei soldiers, and linked up with Taizu at Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 遷滑州牢城遏後指揮使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to commander of the hind-guard “Hold-the-Walls” unit at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to commander of Huazhou’s Hold-the-Walls rear guard.

sentences.zh: 梁兵攻鄆，存節使都將王言藏船鄆西北隅濠中，期以日午渡兵逾濠急攻之。

translations.literal: Liang attacked Yan; Cunjie had his commander Wang Yan hide boats in the moat at Yan’s northwest corner, planning to cross at noon and storm the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang besieged Yan, Cunjie hid boats in the northwest moat under Commander Wang Yan, planning a noon crossing for a sudden assault.

sentences.zh: 會營中火起，鄆人登城望火，言伏不敢動，與存節失期，存節獨破鄆西甕城門，奪其濠橋，梁兵得俱進，遂破朱宣。

translations.literal: A fire broke out in camp; Yan’s men climbed the wall to watch; Yan dared not move and missed the rendezvous; Cunjie alone broke Yan’s western barbican gate, seized the moat bridge, Liang’s army poured in, and Zhu Xuan was broken.
translations.idiomatic: A camp fire broke out; Yan’s defenders climbed the walls to watch; Wang Yan stayed hidden and missed the hour; Cunjie alone stormed the western barbican, seized the moat bridge, and Liang’s whole force poured in and broke Zhu Xuan.

sentences.zh: 從葛從周攻淮南，從周敗渒河，存節收其散卒八千以歸。

translations.literal: Following Ge Congzhou against Huainan, when Congzhou was defeated at the Bi River, Cunjie gathered eight thousand scattered troops and returned.
translations.idiomatic: With Ge Congzhou on the Huainan campaign, after Congzhou’s defeat on the Bi River Cunjie gathered eight thousand scattered men and brought them home.

sentences.zh: 拜亳、宿二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Bo and Su.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Bo and Su.

sentences.zh: 朱瑾走吳，召吳兵攻徐、宿，存節謀曰：「淮兵必不先攻宿，然宿溝壘素固，可以禦敵。

translations.literal: Zhu Jin fled to Wu and summoned Wu troops to attack Xu and Su; Cunjie planned: “Huainan troops will surely not attack Su first; yet Su’s trenches and walls are strong and can hold off the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jin fled to Wu and brought Wu troops against Xu and Su; Cunjie judged: “The Huainan army won’t hit Su first—but Su’s trenches and walls are strong enough to hold.

sentences.zh: 」乃夜以兵急趣徐州，比傅徐城下，瑾兵方至，望其塵起，驚曰：「梁兵已來，何其速也！

translations.literal: ” He then rushed troops by night toward Xuzhou; reaching the walls before Zhu Jin’s army arrived, they saw the dust and cried in alarm: “Liang troops are already here—how fast!
translations.idiomatic: ” He raced by night toward Xuzhou; his dust was rising under the walls when Jin’s army arrived—they cried: “Liang is here already—how fast!

sentences.zh: 」不能攻而去。

translations.literal: ” Unable to attack, they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: ” They could not attack and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 已而太祖使者至，授存節軍機，悉與存節意合，由是諸將益服其能。

translations.literal: Soon Taizu’s envoy arrived and gave Cunjie military authority; it all matched Cunjie’s thinking, and from this the generals respected his ability the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu’s messenger came and handed Cunjie field command, every order matched his own plans—the generals came to trust his judgment even more.

sentences.zh: 遷潞州都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Lu Prefecture as chief commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief commander at Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太祖攻鳳翔，使召存節。

translations.literal: When Taizu attacked Fengxiang he summoned Cunjie.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu besieged Fengxiang he called for Cunjie.

sentences.zh: 存節為將，法令嚴整而善得士心，潞人送者皆號泣。

translations.literal: Cunjie as a commander had strict discipline yet won the men’s hearts; the people of Lu who saw him off all wept aloud.
translations.idiomatic: Cunjie ran a tight camp yet won his men’s hearts; the people of Lu who saw him off wept as he left.

sentences.zh: 累拜邢州團練使、元帥府左都押衙。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed regimental commissioner of Xing and Left Chief Escort of the Marshal’s Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to regimental commissioner of Xing and Left Chief Escort of the Marshal’s Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 同州劉知俊叛，奔鳳翔，乃遷存節匡國軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Tong Prefecture’s Liu Zhijun rebelled and fled to Fengxiang, Cunjie was moved to military governor of the Kuangguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhijun of Tongzhou rebelled and fled to Fengxiang; Cunjie was sent to govern the Kuangguo Army.

sentences.zh: 友珪立，朱友謙叛附於晉，西連鳳翔，存節東西受敵。

translations.literal: When Yougui took the throne, Zhu Youqian rebelled and joined Jin, linking west with Fengxiang; Cunjie was attacked from east and west.
translations.idiomatic: When Yougui seized the throne, Zhu Youqian defected to Jin and tied west to Fengxiang; Cunjie was squeezed from both directions.

sentences.zh: 同州水咸而無井，知俊叛梁，以渴不能守而走，故友謙與岐兵合圍持久，欲以渴疲之，存節禱而擇地鑿井八十，水皆甘可食，友謙卒不能下。

translations.literal: Tong’s water was brackish and there were no wells; when Zhijun rebelled against Liang he could not hold out for thirst and fled—so Youqian and the Qi troops besieged long, hoping to wear them out with thirst; Cunjie prayed, chose ground, and dug eighty wells; the water was sweet and drinkable; Youqian could not take the city.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhou’s water was brackish and there were no wells; Zhijun had fled Liang because thirst broke him—so Youqian and the Qi army settled in for a long siege to starve them of water; Cunjie prayed, chose ground, and sunk eighty wells—all sweet; Youqian never took the city.

sentences.zh: 末帝立，加同中書門下平章事，徙鎮天平。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, Cunjie was made co-equal of the Secretariat and transferred to Tianshang.
translations.idiomatic: At the Last Emperor’s accession Cunjie became co-equal of the Secretariat and was posted to Tianshang.

sentences.zh: 蔣殷反徐州，遣存節攻破之，以功加太尉。

translations.literal: When Jiang Yin rebelled at Xuzhou, Cunjie was sent to break him; for merit he was promoted to Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yin rebelled at Xuzhou; Cunjie was sent to crush him and rose to Grand Commander for the deed.

sentences.zh: 梁、晉相距於河上，存節病痟，而梁、晉方苦戰，存節忠憤彌激，治軍督士，未嘗言病。

translations.literal: Liang and Jin faced each other on the river; Cunjie had chronic dysentery; yet as Liang and Jin fought bitterly, Cunjie’s loyal indignation grew; he drilled the army and never spoke of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Jin locked horns on the river; Cunjie suffered chronic dysentery—yet as the war grew bitter his loyal rage only sharpened; he drilled troops and never mentioned his sickness.

sentences.zh: 病革，召歸京師，將卒，語其子知業曰：「忠孝，吾子也。

translations.literal: As his illness worsened he was recalled to the capital; dying, he said to his son Zhiye: “Loyal and filial—you are my son.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness turned grave he was recalled to the capital; dying, he told his son Zhiye: “Loyal and filial—that is my son.

sentences.zh: 」不及其佗。

translations.literal: ” He said no more.
translations.idiomatic: ” He said nothing else.

sentences.zh: 贈太師。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 張歸霸

translations.literal: Zhang Guiba
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guiba

sentences.zh: （弟歸厚歸弁）〉

translations.literal: (with younger brothers Guihou and Guibian appended)〉
translations.idiomatic: (with younger brothers Guihou and Guibian appended)〉

sentences.zh: 張歸霸，清河人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Guiba was a native of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guiba came from Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 末帝娶其女，是為德妃。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor married his daughter, who became Consort De.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor took his daughter as consort—Consort De.

sentences.zh: 歸霸少與其弟歸厚、歸弁俱從黃巢，巢敗東走，歸霸兄弟乃降梁。

translations.literal: Guiba in youth with his younger brothers Guihou and Guibian followed Huang Chao; when Chao was defeated and fled east, the Zhang brothers submitted to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: As youths Guiba and his brothers Guihou and Guibian followed Huang Chao; when Chao broke and fled east they surrendered to Liang.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權攻汴，歸霸戰數有功。

translations.literal: When Qin Zongquan attacked Bian, Guiba fought with repeated merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Zongquan struck Bian, Guiba fought bravely and often.

sentences.zh: 張至軍赤岡，以騎兵挑戰，矢中歸霸，歸霸拔之，反以射賊，一發而斃，奪其馬而歸。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhi’s army was at Chigang; cavalry challenged; an arrow struck Guiba; Guiba pulled it out, shot back, and killed with one shot, seized the man’s horse and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Chigang Zhang Zhi’s cavalry challenged; an arrow hit Guiba; he pulled it out, fired back, dropped his man with one shot, took his horse, and rode home.

sentences.zh: 太祖從高丘望見，甚壯之，賞以金帛，並以其馬賜之。

translations.literal: Taizu saw from a high mound and was greatly impressed; rewarded him with gold and silk and gave him the horse as well.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu watched from a height and was thrilled; he showered Guiba with gold and silk and gave him the captured horse too.

sentences.zh: 使以弓手五百人伏湟中，太祖以騎數百為遊兵，過至柵，至出兵追太祖，歸霸發伏，殺至兵千人，奪馬數十匹。

translations.literal: He had five hundred archers lie in ambush in the Huang; Taizu with several hundred cavalry acted as skirmishers; passing Zhang Zhi’s stockade, Zhi sent troops to pursue Taizu; Guiba sprang the ambush, killed a thousand of Zhi’s men, seized dozens of horses.
translations.idiomatic: He hid five hundred archers in the Huang reed beds; Taizu rode out with a few hundred cavalry as bait; passing Zhang Zhi’s palisade, Zhi sent men after him; Guiba sprung the trap, killed a thousand, and took dozens of horses.

sentences.zh: 子漢傑，事末帝為顯官，以張德妃故用事。

translations.literal: His son Hanjie served the Last Emperor in high office and wielded power because of Consort Zhang De.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hanjie held high office under the Last Emperor and ran affairs through Consort De.

sentences.zh: 梁亡，唐莊宗入汴，遂族誅。

translations.literal: When Liang fell and Tang’s Zhuangzong entered Bian, the whole clan was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang fell and Zhuangzong of Tang took Bian, the clan was wiped out to the last man.

sentences.zh: 弟歸厚

translations.literal: Younger brother Guihou
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Guihou

sentences.zh: 弟歸厚，字德坤。

translations.literal: The younger brother Guihou, styled Dekun.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Guihou, styled Dekun.

sentences.zh: 為將善用弓槊，能以少擊眾。

translations.literal: As a general he was skilled with bow and spear and could strike many with few.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander he excelled with bow and spear and could beat larger forces with fewer men.

sentences.zh: 張至屯赤岡，歸厚與至獨戰陣前，至憊而卻，諸將乘之，至遂大敗。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhi camped at Chigang; Guihou fought Zhi alone before the lines; Zhi tired and retreated; the generals pressed; Zhi was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhi held Chigang; Guihou met him alone in front of the lines; Zhi tired and fell back; the other generals piled on and Zhi was routed.

sentences.zh: 太祖大悅，以為騎長。

translations.literal: Taizu rejoiced greatly and made him cavalry captain.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was delighted and made him cavalry captain.

sentences.zh: 梁攻時溥，歸厚以麾下先進九里山，遇徐兵而戰，梁故將陳璠叛在徐，歸厚望見識之，瞋目大罵，馳騎直往取之，矢中其左目。

translations.literal: Liang attacked Shi Pu; Guihou led his troops ahead at Jiuli Mountain, met Xu troops and fought; former Liang general Chen Fan had rebelled and was at Xu; Guihou saw and recognized him, glared and cursed, charged straight at him, and an arrow struck his left eye.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang’s assault on Shi Pu, Guihou led the van at Jiuli Mountain and met Xu troops; Chen Fan, a former Liang general now at Xu, was spotted—Guihou glared, cursed, and spurred straight at him; an arrow took his left eye.

sentences.zh: 郴王友裕攻鄆，屯濮州，太祖從後至，友裕徙柵，與太祖相失。

translations.literal: Prince Chen Youyu attacked Yan and camped at Puzhou; Taizu came from behind; Youyu moved his stockade and lost contact with Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chen Youyu besieged Yan from Puzhou; Taizu came up from the rear; Youyu shifted camp and lost touch with Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太祖卒與鄆兵遇，太祖登高望之，鄆兵才千人，太祖與歸厚以廳子軍直沖之，戰已合，鄆兵大至，歸厚度不能支，以數十騎衛太祖先還。

translations.literal: Taizu suddenly met Yan troops; Taizu climbed high to look; Yan had only a thousand men; Taizu and Guihou charged straight with the palace guard; battle joined, Yan reinforcements arrived in force; Guihou could barely hold; with several dozen cavalry he escorted Taizu back first.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu suddenly ran into Yan troops, climbed a rise to look—only a thousand men; he and Guihou charged with the palace guard; as battle joined Yan reinforcements poured in; Guihou could barely hold and rode back first with a few dozen cavalry to shield Taizu.

sentences.zh: 歸厚馬中矢僵，乃持槊步鬥。

translations.literal: Guihou’s horse was struck by an arrow and fell; he took his spear and fought on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Guihou’s horse took an arrow and collapsed; he took up his spear and fought on foot.

sentences.zh: 太祖還軍中，遣張筠馳騎第取之，以為必死矣。

translations.literal: Taizu returned to camp and sent Zhang Yun riding hard to take him first, thinking him surely dead.
translations.idiomatic: Back in camp Taizu sent Zhang Yun galloping to rescue him, sure he was dead.

sentences.zh: 歸厚體被十餘箭，得筠馬乃歸，太祖見之，泣曰：「爾在，喪軍何足計乎！

translations.literal: Guihou’s body bore more than ten arrows; he got Yun’s horse and returned; Taizu saw him and wept: “As long as you live, what matter if an army is lost!
translations.idiomatic: More than ten arrows pierced Guihou; he seized Yun’s horse and made it back; Taizu saw him and wept: “You’re alive—what is the loss of an army!

sentences.zh: 」使舁歸宣武。

translations.literal: ” He had him carried back to Xuanyi.
translations.idiomatic: ” He had him carried home to Xuanyi.

sentences.zh: 遷右神武統軍，歷洺、晉、絳三州刺史。

translations.literal: Promoted to commander of the Right Divine Martial Army, he served as prefect of Ming, Jin, and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to commander of the Right Divine Martial and governed Ming, Jin, and Jiang in turn.

sentences.zh: 與晉人屢戰未嘗屈。

translations.literal: Fighting Jin repeatedly he was never broken.
translations.idiomatic: In repeated clashes with Jin he never broke.

sentences.zh: 乾化元年，拜鎮國軍節度使，以疾卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianhua he was made military governor of the Zhenguo Army and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianhua 1 he was made governor of the Zhenguo Army and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 子漢卿。

translations.literal: Son Hanqing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hanqing.

sentences.zh: 弟歸弁

translations.literal: Younger brother Guibian
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Guibian

sentences.zh: 歸弁，為將亦善戰，開平初為滑州長劍指揮使。

translations.literal: Guibian as a general was also skilled in battle; at the start of Kaiping he was Long-Sword commander at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guibian fought well too; early in Kaiping he commanded Huazhou’s Long-Sword unit.

sentences.zh: 子漢融。

translations.literal: Son Hanrong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hanrong.

sentences.zh: 梁亡，皆族誅。

translations.literal: When Liang fell, all were executed clan by clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang fell, they too were wiped out to the last man.

sentences.zh: 王重師

translations.literal: Wang Chongshi
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongshi

sentences.zh: 王重師，許州長社人也。

translations.literal: Wang Chongshi was a native of Changshe in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongshi came from Changshe in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 為人沈嘿多智，善劍槊。

translations.literal: By nature silent and deep, full of wisdom, skilled with sword and spear.
translations.idiomatic: Silent and shrewd, he was master of sword and spear.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權陷許州，重師脫身歸梁，從太祖平蔡，攻兗、鄆，為拔山軍指揮使。

translations.literal: When Qin Zongquan took Xuzhou, Chongshi escaped to Liang, followed Taizu to pacify Cai, attacked Yan and Yanzhou, and became commander of the “Uproot-Mountains” Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Zongquan seized Xuzhou, Chongshi slipped away to Liang, followed Taizu against Cai, stormed Yan and Yanzhou, and commanded the Uproot-Mountains Army.

sentences.zh: 重師苦戰齊、魯間，威震鄰敵。

translations.literal: Chongshi fought bitterly between Qi and Lu; his prestige shook neighboring foes.
translations.idiomatic: Chongshi fought hard across Qi and Lu, and his name terrified the neighboring realms.

sentences.zh: 遷潁州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Ying.

sentences.zh: 太祖攻濮州，已破，濮人積草焚之，梁兵不得入。

translations.literal: Taizu attacked Puzhou; it was broken; Puzhou men piled grass and burned it; Liang troops could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu took Puzhou, but the defenders piled grass and set fires—Liang’s men could not get in.

sentences.zh: 是時，重師方病金瘡，臥帳中，諸將強之，重師遽起，悉取軍中氈毯沃以水，蒙之火上，率精卒以短兵突入，梁兵隨之皆入，遂取濮州。

translations.literal: At the time Chongshi had a suppurating wound and lay in his tent; the generals urged him; Chongshi sprang up, took all the army’s felt blankets, soaked them in water, covered the fire, led elite troops with short weapons to burst in, Liang troops followed all in, and took Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chongshi lay in his tent with a festering wound; the generals dragged him up; he soaked every felt blanket in camp, threw them on the flames, and led elite troops in with short blades—the whole army poured after him and took Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 重師身被八九瘡，軍士負之而還。

translations.literal: Chongshi’s body bore eight or nine wounds; soldiers carried him back.
translations.idiomatic: Eight or nine wounds covered his body; his men carried him out.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，驚曰：「柰何使我得濮州而失重師乎！

translations.literal: Taizu heard and cried in alarm: “How can I gain Puzhou yet lose Chongshi!
translations.idiomatic: Taizu heard and cried: “I win Puzhou but lose Chongshi—how can that be!

sentences.zh: 」使醫理之，逾月乃愈。

translations.literal: ” He sent doctors to treat him; after more than a month he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent physicians; after a month Chongshi healed.

sentences.zh: 王師範降，表重師青州留後，累遷佑國軍節度使、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Wang Shifan submitted, Chongshi was recommended as Qingzhou acting governor; he rose to military governor of the Youguo Army and co-equal of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shifan surrendered, Chongshi was made acting governor of Qingzhou and rose to governor of the Youguo Army and co-equal of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 居數年，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: After several years he wielded great prestige and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: For years he ruled with stern prestige and real kindness.

sentences.zh: 重師與劉捍故有隙，捍嘗構之太祖，太祖疑之。

translations.literal: Chongshi and Liu Han had an old grudge; Han had slandered him to Taizu; Taizu grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Chongshi and Liu Han bore an old grudge; Han had whispered against him, and Taizu began to doubt.

sentences.zh: 重師遣其將張君練西攻邠、鳳而不先請，君練兵小敗，太祖以其擅發兵，挫失國威，將召而罪之，遣劉捍代重師。

translations.literal: Chongshi sent his general Zhang Junlian west against Bin and Feng without asking first; Junlian’s troops suffered a small defeat; Taizu, holding that unauthorized deployment had shamed the state, planned to summon and punish him, and sent Liu Han to replace Chongshi.
translations.idiomatic: Chongshi sent Zhang Junlian west against Bin and Feng without permission; Junlian lost a skirmish; Taizu, calling it an unauthorized blow to the realm’s prestige, moved to punish him and sent Liu Han to replace Chongshi.

sentences.zh: 重師不知太祖怒己，捍至，重師不出迎，見之青門，禮又倨，捍因馳白太祖，言重師有二誌。

translations.literal: Chongshi did not know Taizu was angry; when Han arrived Chongshi did not come out to greet him; meeting him at the Green Gate his courtesy was haughty; Han raced to tell Taizu that Chongshi had two hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Chongshi did not know Taizu was angry; when Han arrived he stayed inside; at the Green Gate his greeting was cold and proud; Han galloped to Taizu and said Chongshi had two hearts.

sentences.zh: 太祖益怒，貶重師溪州刺史，再貶崖州司戶參軍，未行，賜死。

translations.literal: Taizu grew angrier; demoted Chongshi to prefect of Xi, then again to registrar at Yazhou; before he could go, he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu’s fury deepened; Chongshi was demoted to prefect of Xi, then again to registrar at Yazhou; before he could depart, he was ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 徐懷玉

translations.literal: Xu Huaiyu
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huaiyu

sentences.zh: 徐懷玉，亳州焦夷人也。

translations.literal: Xu Huaiyu was a native of Jiaoyi in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huaiyu came from Jiaoyi in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 少事梁太祖，與太祖俱起微賤。

translations.literal: In youth he served Liang Taizu; both rose from humble beginnings.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served Liang Taizu—they had risen together from nothing.

sentences.zh: 懷玉為將，以雄豪自任，而勇於戰陣。

translations.literal: Huaiyu as a general took himself for a bold hero and was brave in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyu styled himself a bold hero and fought fearlessly in the line.

sentences.zh: 從太祖鎮宣武，為永城鎮將。

translations.literal: Following Taizu when he held Xuanyi, he was garrison commander of Yongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu held Xuanyi, Huaiyu commanded the garrison at Yongcheng.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權攻梁，壁金堤、靈昌、酸棗，懷玉以輕騎連擊破之，俘殺五千餘人，遷左長劍都虞候。

translations.literal: Qin Zongquan attacked Liang, fortifying Jindi, Lingchang, and Suanzao; Huaiyu with light cavalry repeatedly broke them, captured and killed more than five thousand, and was promoted to Left Long-Sword Chief Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan attacked Liang and walled himself at Jindi, Lingchang, and Suanzao; Huaiyu routed him again and again with light cavalry, killed or captured more than five thousand, and rose to Left Long-Sword Chief Inspector.

sentences.zh: 又破宗權於板橋、赤岡，拔其八柵。

translations.literal: He again defeated Zongquan at Banqiao and Chigang, taking eight stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He beat Zongquan again at Banqiao and Chigang and tore down eight stockades.

sentences.zh: 從太祖東攻兗、鄆，破徐、宿。

translations.literal: Following Taizu east to attack Yan and Yanzhou, he broke Xu and Su.
translations.idiomatic: With Taizu east against Yan and Yanzhou he broke Xu and Su.

sentences.zh: 懷玉金創被體，戰必克捷，所得賞賚，往往以分士卒，為梁名將。

translations.literal: Huaiyu’s body was covered with battle wounds; he always won in fight; rewards he often divided among the troops; he was a famed Liang general.
translations.idiomatic: Wounds covered Huaiyu’s body; he always won; he split his rewards among the ranks—and became one of Liang’s great generals.

sentences.zh: 本名琮，太祖賜名懷玉。

translations.literal: His original name was Cong; Taizu bestowed the name Huaiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Born Cong, he received the name Huaiyu from Taizu.

sentences.zh: 從太祖攻魏，敗魏兵黎陽，遂東攻兗，破朱瑾於金鄉。

translations.literal: Following Taizu against Wei, defeated Wei troops at Liyang, then attacked east toward Yan, broke Zhu Jin at Jinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: With Taizu against Wei he crushed Wei at Liyang, then swung east, and broke Zhu Jin at Jinxiang.

sentences.zh: 又從龐師古攻楊行密，師古敗清口，懷玉獨完一軍，行收散卒萬餘人以歸。

translations.literal: Again with Pang Shigu against Yang Xingmi; Shigu was defeated at Qingkou; Huaiyu alone preserved a whole army, then gathered more than ten thousand scattered troops on the march home.
translations.idiomatic: With Pang Shigu against Yang Xingmi, after Shigu’s rout at Qingkou Huaiyu saved an entire army whole, then gathered more than ten thousand scattered men on the march home.

sentences.zh: 遷沂州刺史，屬歲屢豐，乃繕兵治壁，為戰守具。

translations.literal: Transferred to prefect of Yi; harvests ran rich for years; he repaired troops and walls and prepared for war and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Made prefect of Yi, he used several fat harvest years to drill troops, repair walls, and stock the frontier for war.

sentences.zh: 已而王師範叛梁，攻東境，懷玉屢以州兵擊破之。

translations.literal: Later Wang Shifan rebelled against Liang and attacked the eastern border; Huaiyu repeatedly broke him with prefecture troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shifan rebelled and struck the eastern marches, Huaiyu beat him again and again with his own prefectural force.

sentences.zh: 遷齊州防禦使。

translations.literal: Transferred to defense commissioner of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was made defense commissioner of Qi.

sentences.zh: 天復四年，以州兵遼昭宗都洛陽，遷華州觀察留後，以兵屯雍州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianfu, with prefecture troops he escorted Emperor Zhaozong to Luoyang, was made acting observation commissioner of Huazhou, and garrisoned troops at Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 4 he led Qi troops to escort Emperor Zhaozong to Luoyang, became acting governor of Huazhou, and posted his army at Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷右羽林統軍，屯於澤州，晉人攻之，為隧以入，懷玉擊之隧中，晉人乃卻。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Imperial Guard commander, encamped at Ze Prefecture; Jin forces attacked, dug a tunnel to enter, Huaiyu struck them in the tunnel, and the Jin forces then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander of the Right Imperial Guard and encamped at Zezhou; when Jin troops attacked and dug a tunnel under the walls, Huaiyu met them inside and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，歷曹、晉二州刺史，晉數攻之，懷玉堅守，敗晉兵於洪洞。

translations.literal: In Taizu’s time he successively served as prefect of Cao and Jin; Jin repeatedly attacked; Huaiyu held firm and defeated Jin troops at Hongdong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizu he served as prefect of Cao and Jin in turn; Jin attacked again and again, but Huaiyu held both posts and routed Jin forces at Hongdong.

sentences.zh: 拜保大軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was appointed military governor of the Baoda Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military governor of the Baoda Army.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，友珪自立，朱友謙附於晉，以襲鄜州，執懷玉殺之。

translations.literal: When Taizu died, Yougui declared himself ruler; Zhu Youqian attached himself to Jin and raided Fu Prefecture, seized Huaiyu, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu died and Yougui seized the throne, Zhu Youqian went over to Jin and struck Fu Prefecture, captured Huaiyu, and killed him.
